MENT OFFICER 1 
(lABORIE)
Qualifications :
Applicants should possess:
Bachelor’s Degree in Social Work, 
Community Development or Sociology, 
plus two (2) years experience in a post 
at Grade 10 and above 
or
Bachelor’s Degree in Social Work, Com-
munity Development or Sociology, plus 
eight (8) years total experience in a post 
at Grade 7 and above
or
Diploma in Social Work, Community 
Development or Sociology plus three (3) 
years experience in a post at Grade 10 
and above.
Computer literacy, experience in com-
munity work and ability to communicate 
effectively in English and Patois 
especially at the group and community 
level would be an asset.
Duties and Responsibilities:
The successful applicant will be 
required to work under the direction of 
and report to the Assistant Director of 
Community Services and Local Gov-
ernment.  He/she will also respond to 
the Director of Community Services and 
Local Government on matters related to 
work in progress.  
The applicant will be required to:
mobilize, motivate and organize com-mu-
nities towards the development of com-
munity actions;
facilitate communities and Local 
Government Authorities in acquiring skills 
in needs assessment, resource identifi-
cation, project planning, implementation 
and evaluation;
facilitate the establishment and 
development of community groups and 
assist in providing the support services 
necessary for their effectiveness;
organize and facilitate the conduct 
of non-formal education/training pro-
grammes in keeping with the needs of 
the respective communities.
organize and promote community 
development projects and programmes 
in response to community needs;
promote self-help as a tool of com-munity 
development;
assist in the identification and develop-
ment of projects and programmes aimed 
at poverty alleviation/eradication;
ensure community awareness, prepared-
ness for disasters and mitigation plans;
assist communities in acquisition of 
requisite management skills for the 
management and maintenance of 
infra-structural facilities;
assist Council(s) in planning and im-
plementing work programmes and 
attend Council meetings as an ex-officio 
member;
document community development 
processes;
any other related duty as may be 
assigned from time to time by the 
Director and Assistant Director, Com-mu-
nity Services and Local Government.
Skills, Knowledge and Abilities:
The applicant should:

CIVIL  ENGINEER
Qualification:
Applicants should possess:
Level I
A Degree in Civil Engineering or 
Structural Engineering plus two (2) years 
working experience in a related field 
and Postgraduate qualifications in Civil 
Engineering or equivalent.
Level II
As for Level 1, plus four (4) years 
experience in a related field.
Level III
As for Level 1, plus four (5) years expe-
rience in a related field.
Duties and Responsibilities:
The successful applicant will be 
required to work under the direction of 
and report to the Chief Physical Planner 
and is required to respond whenever 
necessary to the Director of Planning on 
matters related to work in progress. He 
or she is expected to:
examine and advise on physical develop-
ment plans prepared in respect of water 
reticulation systems, drainage schemes, 
sewerage disposal plants and road net-
work engineering;
prepare plans for public water supply, 
solid waste  disposal. Public drainage, 
sewage disposal and flood control;
conduct research on environmental, 
structural and civil engineering issues;
review building construction plans in 
respect of structural and engineering 
details, surface and storm drainage, water 
supply and solid waste disposal;
examine land development plans in 
respect of drainage systems, road 
engineering, soil stability and other 
engineering aspects of land development;
advise the Section and Develop-
ment Control Authority (DCA)  on all 
engineering matters and provide repre-
sentation on all agencies and bodies in 
addition to co-ordination the engineering 
function of the section;
assess the adequacy of ongoing or com-
pleted road and drainage infrastructure 
works in land subdivisions relative to the 
Performance Bond requirements and 
other conditions of approval;
enforce the provisions of the Building 
Code and Guideline in development 
planning applications and in building 
construction and land development 
practice;
conduct Engineering Impact Assess-
ments of development projects and 
review and advise on the engineering 
component of Environmental Impact 
Statements;
undertake geo-technical studies, which 
may be required to determine land de-
velopment  issues resulting from devel-
opment planning applications;
present and defend engineering plans 
before in-house Committees or members 
of the DCA as required;
prepare an annual work programme and 
a quarterly progress report on the work 
programme for submission to the Chief 
Physical Planner;
perform such other duties as may be 
assigned from time to time by the Chief 
Physical Planner or Director of Planning.
Conditions:
The successful applicant will be 
required to function in a scheduled 
traveling post and will be required to 
maintain a motor vehicle for the prop-
er performance of duties. He/She will 
receive basic traveling allowance and 
mileage allowance in accordance with 
approved rates.

FIELD NUTRITION OFFICER I
Qualification :
Applicants should possess: 
Diploma in Nutrition and Dietetics from a 
recognised institution
	
	
	
	
Duties and Responsibilities:
The successful applicant will be 
required to report and work under the 
direction of the Nutritionist.  He/she will 
also be required to respond whenever 
necessary to the Permanent Secretary 
or Deputy Permanent Secretary, Ministry 
of Health, Human Services and Family 
Affairs, on matters related to work in 
progress.
The applicant will be required to:
work in collaboration with the Nutri-
tionist to implement a nutrition 
education programme to improve the 
nutritional status of the community;
plan, develop, supervise, monitor 
and evaluate nutrition services in an 
assigned geographic area as part of the 
national nutrition programme;
co-ordinate within the geographic area, 
nutrition services with other operating 
programmes of the Ministry to which 
assigned and with related programmes 
of other Ministries;
participate in the preparation, review, 
selection and development of nutrition 
educational materials and techniques for 
dissemination of nutrition information to 
professional and non-professional audi-
ences through the mass media;
investigate food habits and conducts 
simple dietary surveys to determine 
eating practices of the community service 
and the cultural and socio-economic fac-
tors influencing these practices;
demonstrate methods of preparation 
of nutritious foods in clinics and/or 
community centres to groups within the 
assigned area;
lecture to students in nursing, public 
health inspection, other allied health 
workers and agricultural extension 
officers, as assigned;
provide nutrition consultation to 
physicians, nurses, social workers, 
teachers, agricultural extension officers, 
community development workers and 
other professional workers on current 
nutrition research finding and the practical 
application to personal community health;
make home visits to assist individu-
als or families with menu planning, 
food purchasing, food storage and 
food preparation skills, with a view to 
improving the nutritional value of their 
diets;
provide assistance to group feed-
ing programmes within the assigned 
community, advising on menus, food 
purchasing, preparation and storage 
methods and other food and nutrition-re-
lated aspects of the programme, e.g. 
Day Care Centres, “Meals-on-Wheels”, 
School Feeding Programmes, Resident 
Homes for children and the elderly;
report and summarize progress and activ-
ities at regular intervals, prepare periodic 
and special reports;
evaluate programmes in terms of objec-
tives and collaborates with Nutritionist in 
developing plans for the future.
Skills, Knowledge and Abilities:
The applicants should have:
knowledge of human nutrition in health 
disease;
knowledge of research methods and 
survey techniques used in assessment 
of nutritional status;
knowledge of principles of food service 
management;
knowledge of environmental and home 
conditions in community served by 
the Ministry and of the problems and 
attitudes of people residing there.  Ability 
to collect and maintain nutrition data;
ability to establish and maintain effective 
and harmonious working relations with 
individuals, families, community groups, 
Ministry of Health staff and staff of other 
relevant ministries;
ability to plan, interpret and promote the 
national food and nutrition programme.
Salary:
Salary is in the range of $22,875.84 - 
$25,401.60 per annum (Grade 6).

along with references and certified 
copies of documents pertaining to qualifi-
cations should be addressed to:
The Secretary
Public Service Commission

Castries

CASTRIES  BASIN  COMMUNITIES
T
HE general public is hereby informed 
of the commencement of a 
Reconnaissance Survey of the many 
communities located within the Castries 
Basin, particularly those located in the 
upper levels of the catchment.
The purpose for this survey is to provide 
the Ministry of Physical Development, 
Environment & Housing with a better 
appreciation of the housing, land-use and 
related social issues and infrastructure in 
those communities.
Residents within the Castries Basin are 
therefore kindly requested to cooperate 
fully with the Ministry’s officials, who 
will be visiting your community and 
households, commencing 16 February 
2004. Ultimately, the main objective is to 
develop project proposals that seek to 
improve the quality of life for residents and 
the various communities in the Castries 
Basin.

POST OFFICE NOTICE
25th Anniversary 
of Saint Lucia’s 
Independence
T
HE public is informed that an issue of 
stamps commemorating the 25th 
Anniversary of Saint Lucia’s 
Independence will be released for sale 
at all post office outlets on Friday 20th 
February, 2004.
The issue comprises a set of four stamps 
as follows:
20c – captures the moment at midnight 
when the union jack was lowered 
for the last time and Saint Lucia’s 
Flag was raised for the first time. 
	
Standing by is HRH Princess Alex-
andra (representative of HRH Queen 
Elizabeth II) with Saint  Lucia’s first 
Prime Minister, The Right Honourable 
John Compton.
95c – depicts a composite of indus-
tries including air and sea trade, 
	
Tourism, the Banana Industry 
	
(representing the Agricultural 
	
Sector) and the ‘people’ represent-
ed by a boy and girl reading the 
alle-gorical Book of Knowledge. 
The square rigged ship depicts the 
	
pioneering history of the island when 
sailing vessels were the only means 
of communication between nations 
and Saint Lucia provided a ‘safe 
anchorage for ships’ in the Harbour 
of Castries.
$1.10 – shows the 25th Anniversary 
	
symbol framed in green banana 
leaves against a mauve background.
$5.00 – depicts the Castries Harbour with 
four mega ships berthed alongside 
the several deep-water wharves of 
which Sainty Lucia is so famous, ever 
since the days of steam when the 
harbour was a bustling coaling depot 
that ranked 13th in the whole of the 
British Empire at the time.
Souvenir Sheets
Souvenir Sheets will not be available.
First Day Covers
First Day Covers are available at a cost 
of $10.25 each.
First Day of Issue Postmark
All letters posted up to mid-night on 
Friday 20th February, 2004 will receive 
the first day of issue postmark.
The stamps will remain on sale for a period 
of six months or until stock is exhausted, 
whichever is the sooner.

Independence Celebrations in New York
P
rime Minister Dr. Kenny Anthony will on Saturday, February 28, 2004 deliver the feature address at a gala ceremony at 
Flushing Meadow Park in Queens, New York in observance of St. Lucia’s 25th Independence Anniversary. 
The independence ball is also being held as a fundraising event for the Desmond George Memorial Scholarship Fund, established 
to assist needy St. Lucian students in New York. The Mighty Sparrow has agreed to be a guest of honour at this event, which will 
showcase St. Lucian performances, including a ten member section of the Diamond Steel Orchestra and the calypsonian, Invader.
The gala event is part of a packed independence anniversary programme which starts with a church service on Sunday, February 
22nd at 3.00 p.m. at the St. Ignatius Roman Catholic Church. Messages will be delivered on behalf of the Governor General, Her 
Excellency Dame Pearlette Louisy and Prime Minister, Dr. Kenny Anthony.
A special town hall meeting on the subject of immigration and citizenship will be held on Monday, February 23rd, at 6.00 p.m. 
The panel of speakers will be led by Mr. Colin Moore, editor of “The Immigrant” journal, and includes St. Lucians working with 
the United States Immigrant Service and the staff of the St. Lucia High Commission in New York.
On Thursday, February 26th, at 6.00 p.m., Msgr. Dr. Patrick Anthony will deliver a multi- media presentation entitled “The Influence 
of Derek Walcott and His Generation, On the Social, Cultural and Spiritual Life of St. Lucia”. 
A Community Awards ceremony is scheduled for Friday 27th at 6.00 p.m., where a number of St. Lucians will be honoured for 
their contribution to the social and economic development of St. Lucian nationals residing in New York. At this ceremony St. 
Lucian writers, including John Robert Lee, George Fish Alphonse and Anderson Reynolds will present their work. A launching of 
the anthology entitled “Roseau Valley” is also planned for this evening. The Diamond Steel orchestra will perform there.
All the events will be held at the St. Ignatius Church Hall on Rogers Avenue in Brooklyn. 
A highlight of the anniversary celebrations will be the St. Lucian Independence reception at the Untied Nations headquarters, 
where the Diamond Steel orchestra will perform. 
St. Lucia’s ambassador to the United Nations, His Excellency, Anthony Severin says every effort has been made to work with the 
wide range of St. Lucian organisations in New York, including the sports organisations, the Mothers and Fathers Groups and the 
St. Lucia Associations. He stated that there was heightened interest in the activities, and St. Lucians were looking forward for the 
opportunity to meet to discuss immigration and citizenship and the other issues facing St. Lucian and Caribbean communities 
in the United States.

Caribbean out Performs Many Region’s in E-government Readiness
T
he Government of St. Lucia and it’s counterparts from the Caribbean are well
   on their way to providing the much needed environment that would make their 
services more accessible, responsive and cost efficient. St. Lucia’s Com-munications, 
Works, Transport and Public Utilities Minister, Honourable Felix Finisterre made the 
disclosure today, as he addressed a three-day regional workshop on E-Government 
and Sectoral Development at the Cara Suites Hotel in Castries. 
Minister Finisterre told the regional grouping that new information and telecommu-
nication technologies (ITCs) were facilitating the acquisition and adoption of infor-
mation, thereby offering developing states unprecedented opportunities to enhance 
their education systems, improve policy formulation and execution, while expanding 
the possibilities for social change. 
The Caribbean, he said, had proven itself ready to reap the benefits of E-government 
Readiness, placing second only to North America with respect to the human capacity index for e-government, while outperform-
ing regions, such as South and Eastern Asia, South-Central Asia, Western Asia, South and Central America, and Europe. “The 
development of St. Lucia as a service-based or information and knowledge-based economy, therefore, aims at exploiting digital 
technologies to stimulate the achievement of the country’s development objectives,” Minister Finisterre said. 
He noted that the establishment of a knowledge-based society “was the platform on which the region must foster, accelerate and 
sustain long-term social, cultural and economic development.” He admitted however, that much work still needed to be done to 
realize the goal of shaping a new economy, predicated fully on information and communication technologies. 
Government, the Communications Minister pointed out, was seeking to create an enabling environment to attract local and foreign 
investors through appropriate policies, legislation and improved public sector efficiency. That note struck a cord with officials of 
the Commonwealth Secretariat, who are sponsors of the three-day event. “E-government without the culture change becomes 
expensive government and I think we have to focus not so much on the technology, but on the re-engineering of processes, of 
regulations, of information and data sharing, and those are always the tough issues,” said Henry Alamango of the Commonwealth 
Network for Information Technology for Development (COMNET-IT)
E-Government is a concept aimed at encouraging governments to use less ink and paper and more electronic information tech-
nology in their day-to-day affairs.

n an effort to develop project proposals that seek to improve the quality of life of residents in the Castries Basin, the Ministry 
of Physical Development, Environment and Housing is to embark on a comprehensive reconnaissance survey of the many 
communities located in the area. 
Deputy Chief Surveyor Vincent Jn. Baptiste says the survey will provide the Ministry with critical information to help assess the 
market value of selected properties bordering the city centre. These properties are the ones located on the slopes surrounding 
the city and extend from Faux-Au-Chau to upper La Clery, inclusive of the Pavee Lands and Morne-Du-Don. 
The exercise will entail a mass appraisal of these areas, “so that government can in the first instance, rationalized these areas 
and then get an idea as to the monetary value of those properties in the event that a major relocation has to be carried out,” said 
Mr. Jn. Baptiste. The information is expected to go a long way in developing a better appreciation of the housing, land use and 
related social issues and infrastructure in those communities. 
Ultimately the Ministry says the main objective is to develop project proposals that seek to improve the quality of life of residents 
in the Castries Basin. Meantime, residents in the selected areas are being asked to co-operate fully with Ministry personnel in 
conducting the survey.
